skill.name: building-plugins
skill.description: Helps users design, create, validate, document, and publish Claude Code plugins that bundle agents, skills, commands, hooks, and templates into cohesive packages.
skill.summary: Create well-structured Claude Code plugins with validation, packaging, documentation, and publishing guidance.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many high-risk patterns, but review found they are plugin-building documentation, safe templates, or defensive validation checks. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, malicious command execution, prompt injection, destructive filesystem behavior, or covert network activity.

remediation.issue: Shell examples can be copied into real plugins without additional hardening.
remediation.suggestion: Add short notes near shell templates that all user-provided paths and settings must be validated and quoted before use.

remediation.issue: Symlink installation examples write into the Claude plugins directory.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to inspect plugin contents before linking or installing community plugins.

remediation.issue: Template helper scripts may encourage broad filesystem searches.
remediation.suggestion: Limit template searches to the project directory and document expected safe patterns.

content.value_statement: Creating Claude Code plugins requires correct structure, validation, documentation, and safe packaging. This skill guides users through plugin architecture, templates, validation, and publishing workflows.
actual_capabilities: Design plugin layouts that combine agents, skills, commands, hooks, scripts, and README files.
Generate minimal, standard, and full plugin structures from included templates.
Create and validate plugin.json manifests and marketplace metadata.
Explain naming, versioning, distribution, and installation practices for Claude Code plugins.
Run or guide validation checks for plugin structure, JSON syntax, components, and documentation.
Recommend security practices for secrets, tool permissions, scripts, and user configuration files.
limitations: Does not publish plugins automatically without user action and repository access.
Cannot guarantee marketplace acceptance because external review policies may change.
Template scripts still need project-specific review before production use.
Requires users to provide plugin goals, target components, and distribution preferences.

use_cases.title: Create a first plugin
use_cases.description: Generate a small plugin with a manifest, command, README, and installation guidance.

use_cases.title: Package team automations
use_cases.description: Bundle related agents, skills, commands, and hooks into one reusable plugin for a team.

use_cases.title: Prepare marketplace release
use_cases.description: Validate metadata, documentation, versioning, security notes, and distribution files before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a simple plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Claude Code plugin for [goal]. I want the simplest structure with one command and clear installation instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Generate plugin files
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standard Claude Code plugin named [plugin-name] with a plugin.json manifest, README, one command, and one helper script.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an existing plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my plugin directory for manifest errors, missing documentation, unsafe permissions, and publishing blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a full release
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare [plugin-name] for marketplace release. Check versioning, marketplace metadata, security guidance, templates, examples, and migration notes.

output_examples.input: Create a minimal plugin for formatting project notes.
output_examples.output: A proposed plugin structure with a manifest, one command, README sections, installation steps, and validation checklist.

output_examples.input: Validate this plugin before I publish it.
Turn these three commands into a reusable plugin.
output_examples.output: A packaging plan that groups commands, names components consistently, adds metadata, and explains how to test installation.

best_practices: Start with the smallest useful plugin and add components only when they share a clear purpose.
Keep permissions minimal and document any script, network, filesystem, or secret requirements.
Validate manifests, README content, examples, and installation steps before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not bundle unrelated agents, commands, and hooks into one plugin only for convenience.
Do not pre-approve broad tools or destructive actions without a clear user-facing reason.
Do not publish templates that require hidden secrets or undocumented local configuration.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Claude Code plugins that package agents, skills, commands, hooks, scripts, and documentation.

faq.question: Can it create plugin files for me?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create starter structures and templates when you provide the plugin goal and desired components.

faq.question: Does it publish plugins automatically?
faq.answer: No. It prepares files and guidance, but publishing requires user approval and repository access.

faq.question: Can it validate plugin quality?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check structure, manifest fields, documentation, templates, versioning, and common security concerns.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: The guidance targets Claude Code plugins, while the marketplace listing also notes compatibility with Claude and Codex workflows.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the plugin purpose, target users, required components, expected commands, and any distribution plan.
